title: Building curl via cmake ExternalProject_Add does not set CURL_CA_PATH
body:
Hi,

I discovered that CURL_CA_BUNDLE and CURL_CA_PATH does not set properly if I used ExternalProject_Add to build curl as my dependency.

### I did this

The following snippets are how I reproduced this issue. 

```cpp
// a.cc
#include <curl/curl.h>
#include <string>
#include <iostream>

static size_t callback(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, std::string* data)
{
  data->append((char *)ptr, size * nmemb);
  return size * nmemb;
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  auto curl = curl_easy_init();
  std::string resp;

  curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_URL, "https://github.com");
  curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION, callback);
  curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_WRITEDATA, &resp);

  auto rc = curl_easy_perform(curl);
  std::cout << curl_easy_strerror(rc) << "\n";
  std::cout << resp << "\n";
  curl_easy_cleanup(curl);
}
```

```cmake
# CMakeLists.txt

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)
project(test)
set(target test)
file(GLOB SOURCE *.cc)
find_package(OpenSSL REQUIRED)
find_package(ZLIB)

link_directories("${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/lib")

add_executable(${target} ${SOURCE})
add_dependencies(${target} curl)
target_include_directories(${target} PRIVATE "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/include")
target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE curl pthread ZLIB::ZLIB OpenSSL::SSL OpenSSL::Crypto)

include (ExternalProject)
ExternalProject_Add(curl
  GIT_REPOSITORY "https://github.com/curl/curl"
  GIT_TAG "master"
  GIT_CONFIG advice.detachedHead=false
  PREFIX "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/curl"
  CMAKE_CACHE_ARGS
    "-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS:BOOL=OFF"
    "-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}"
)
```

### I expected the following

After running my test program, I expected a response from ``github.com``. However, I received the following error:

Build and run commands:

```bash
$ ls 
a.cc  CMakeLists.txt
$ mkdir build
$ cd build
$ cmake ../
$ make -j 2
$ rm test
$ make -j 2 # run make again
$ ./test
SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK
```

I think the issue is from cmake cache. Probably, we need to ``set(CURL_CA_PATH_SET FALSE) `` and ``set(CURL_CA_BUNDLE_SET FALSE)`` on [CMakeLists.txt:819](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/e052859759b34d0e05ce0f17244873e5cd7b457b/CMakeLists.txt#L819) and [CMakeLists.txt:808](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/e052859759b34d0e05ce0f17244873e5cd7b457b/CMakeLists.txt#L808)?

### curl/libcurl version

master branch

### operating system

ubuntu 20.04
